comparison: Both evaluations address the DNA binding experiments (C23-C25) showing DNA-PK binding to cytoplasmic DNA via affinity purification and mass spectrometry. OpenEval and peer reviewers agree this biochemical evidence is technically sound and well-controlled.

Both evaluations address the immunofluorescence co-localization data (C21, C61-C63, C75) showing DNA-PK components at viral replication sites. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept this observational evidence without challenge.

Both address kinase-independence claims (C54, C89-C91). OpenEval finds the genetic and pharmacological evidence sufficient to support kinase-independent function. Peer reviewers express skepticism, noting surprise at the finding and lack of mechanistic evidence for the proposed scaffolding hypothesis.

Both address STING-Ku70 interaction data (C57-C59) in HEK293 cells. OpenEval finds the immunoprecipitation experiments well-controlled and mechanistically informative. Peer reviewers accept this biochemical evidence without raising concerns.

Both address core DNA sensing phenotype claims (C29-C44) including knockout phenotypes, specificity controls, and rescue experiments. OpenEval finds the multiple lines of evidence sufficient across genotypes. Peer reviewers raise significant concerns about MEF heterogeneity and transformation status, requesting additional complementation experiments beyond Ku80 to rule out artifacts.

Both address DNA-PK's non-redundant role and specificity (C80, C82-C84, C86-C88). OpenEval finds the evidence across genotypes and specificity controls sufficient. Peer reviewers' concerns about MEF heterogeneity and transformation status (from R1) extend to these claims, creating uncertainty about whether effects are specific to DNA-PK loss.

Both address selective gene expression effects (C36-C38). OpenEval considers the data demonstrating consistency across preparations sufficient. Peer reviewers specifically highlight this selective effect as requiring comprehensive microarray analysis to understand the scope and specificity of DNA-PK's role in gene regulation.

Minimal overlap (C2, C22) on DNA virus infection claims. OpenEval finds the viral infection data (C64-C68) demonstrate DNA sensing defects extending to viruses. Peer reviewers' general concerns about MEF heterogeneity and transformation status affect confidence in all phenotypic claims including viral responses.

Minimal overlap (C1) on IRF-3 pathway dependence. OpenEval finds the genetic knockout and immunofluorescence data sufficient to establish DNA-PK upstream of IRF-3. Peer reviewers' concerns about cell line heterogeneity and transformation create uncertainty about pathway claims.
OpenEval evaluated in vivo mouse experiments (C69-C73) showing DNA-specific defects with MVA and HSV-1. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these in vivo claims.
OpenEval evaluated cell-type specificity claims (C76-C79) reconciling findings with prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
OpenEval evaluated novelty claims (C3-C4, C14-C20, C129-C130) contrasting cytoplasmic immune function with nuclear roles. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these novelty arguments.
OpenEval evaluated field context claims (C5-C13) about existing DNA sensors and literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluated acknowledgment of mechanistic gaps (C51, C92-C93). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer concerns about mechanism relate to C54/C89-C91 covered in R2/R4 pairing.
OpenEval evaluated background claims about DNA immunology (C94-C100). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual literature claims.
OpenEval evaluated autoimmunity context claims (C101-C117) including anti-DNA-PK antibodies in disease. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature review claims.
OpenEval evaluated evolutionary context and synthesis claims (C118-C128). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these broader contextual arguments.
